products.summary: The cheapest full-frame 85mm with autofocus for Sony E mount. Reviewers found the center very sharp at f/1.8 on a Sony a7CR, with single-shot AF that is quiet and accurate and continuous AF that locks faster than the price suggests. It focuses to 0.65 m, closer than the original SE's 0.85 m, and has 11 aperture blades for round highlights.
products.fit: Hobbyists on a Sony a7, a7C or a6000-series body who want the 85 mm portrait look for under $200 and shoot mostly stills.
caveats: Soft with visible color fringing at f/1.8 near the close-focus limit; it cleans up by f/4.
Visible focus breathing, so racking focus in video shows the frame change.
Plastic barrel, no aperture ring, no focus-hold button, and only a mount gasket for sealing.
One lab test measured small direction-dependent focus errors; stop down a little for critical work.
Flares broadly into strong light; use the included hood.
Returns go back to China within 7 days, so test it as soon as it arrives.

products.summary: The Nikon Z version of Meike's budget 85mm. A lab test on a Z8 and Z9 measured center resolution of 64.8 lp/mm at f/1.8 and timed focus from 0.8 m to infinity at 0.42 s, faster than a Nikkor 85mm f/1.4 in the same test. Lateral color fringing was among the lowest the tester had seen.
products.fit: Nikon Z6, Z7, Z8, Zf or Z50-series owners who want a fast 85 mm for portraits at a quarter of the Nikkor 85mm f/1.8 S price.
caveats: Focus landed slightly off depending on travel direction in one lab test; stopping down hides it.
Noticeable vignetting at f/1.8 that needs a profile correction.
Focus shifts a few millimeters as you stop down, so focus at the shooting aperture for close work.
Manual focus needs several turns of the ring, which some users dislike.
Only a mount gasket for sealing; not a lens for rain.

products.summary: Meike's step-up 85mm adds a clicked aperture ring, ED glass and a metal build. Fstoppers found tracking smooth without hunting and no focus breathing, which makes it the Meike 85 to pick for video. OpticalLimits rated it decent for the money but wished for more sharpness at f/1.8 on high-resolution bodies.
products.fit: Sony shooters who want an aperture ring and breathing-free focus pulls for video at well under the price of a native 85.
caveats: Costs $140 more than the SE Mark II and focuses less closely (0.85 m).
Could be sharper at f/1.8; peak sharpness is f/4 to f/5.6.
The aperture ring's A position can slip out of auto by accident.
Autofocus is smooth rather than fast; not a sports lens.
Background blur can get busy in cluttered scenes.
